messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Spanish, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Spanish line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
No puedo bien relatar cómo entré, tan lleno estaba de sueño en ese punto donde abandoné la vía verdadera.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑by‑Word Mapping Table (Spanish translation of lines 10‑12)**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|----------------------|--------------------|------------------------|--------| | Io | 1st‑person singular pronoun, subject of “so” | *(omitted)* | I | UNNECESSARY (subject pronoun dropped in Spanish) | | non | negation particle | No | not | OK | | so | verb *sapere* “to know” (present 1 sg) | puedo | can | OK | | ben | adverb of manner “well” | bien | well | OK | | ridir | infinitive “to recount, tell again” | relatar | recount | OK | | com' | interrogative adverb “how” | cómo | how | OK | | i' | clitic pronoun “io” (subject inside clause) | *(omitted)* | I | UNNECESSARY (subject pronoun dropped) | | v'intrai | historic 1 sg “I entered (it)” | entré | entered | OK | | tant' | adverb of degree “so, so much” | tan | so | OK | | era | imperfect 3 sg of *essere* “was” | estaba | was (progressive) | OK | | pien | predicative adjective “full” | lleno | full | OK | | di | preposition linking adjective to noun “of” | de | of | OK | | sonno | noun “sleep, slumber” | sueño | slumber | OK | | a | temporal preposition “at” | en | at | OK | | quel | demonstrative adjective “that” | ese | that | OK | | punto | noun “point, moment” | punto | point | OK | | che | relative pronoun “where” | donde | where | OK | | la | definite article (feminine) “the” | la | the | OK | | verace | adjective “true, genuine” | verdadera | true | OK | | via | noun “way, path” | vía | way | OK | | abbandonai | historic 1 sg “I abandoned” | abandoné | abandoned | OK |
### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: *Io*, *i'* – Spanish normally omits the explicit subject pronoun when the verb is conjugated. - **No other** tokens are missing, wrong, or grammatically mismatched.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Spanish script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Spanish text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).

- **Line 10** - Original: No puedo bien relatar cómo entré, - Issue: Adverb placement (“bien relatar” is non‑standard). - Corrected: **No puedo relatar bien cómo entré,**
- **Line 11** - Original: tan lleno estaba de sueño en ese punto - Issue: Word order (“tan lleno estaba” is awkward). - Corrected: **Estaba tan lleno de sueño en ese punto**
- **Line 12** - Original: donde abandoné la vía verdadera. - Issue: none - Corrected: no change
